newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Lorenzi Diamond buys Japanese company.
newsitem.headline: Israel Lorenzi Diamond buys Japanese company.

text.p: Israel's Lorenzi Diamond Ltd has exercised its option to purchase a 44 percent stake in Japan's jewellery importer Hohrin Co Ltd, a spokesman for Lorenzi said.
Haim Even Zohar said the company's owner Yossi Lorenzi had purchased the stake in the Japanese company on Monday for just below $20 million in cash.
"The deal between Lorenzi and Hohrin will allow the Israeli company to increase its sales to Japan and grow with the Japanese company", he said.
The Japanese company confirmed a Tokyo newspaper report on Tuesday that Lorenzi planned to take a 44 percent stake in the company.
Lorenzi bought the stake from Hohrin founder and former chairman Tadahiko Ura, Even Zohar said.
He said the move will allow Lorenzi to become a major supplier of polished diamonds to Hohrin, but emphasised that existing Israeli suppliers will continue to work with the Japanese company.

Hohrin is a publicly traded company that deals in the sale of polished loose diamonds, diamond studded jewellery and in pearls. The company has a yearly turnover of around $130 million, Even Zohar said.
The Israeli diamond manufacturer, which was the fourth biggest Israeli diamond exporter in 1995 with exports of $71 million, specialises in sales to Far Eastern countries, including Japan.
"The deal is good news for the industry as a whole as it represents a major investment in the diamond field and not outside the field", said Even Zohar.
He said this was the first time Lorenzi has made such a major investment in Japan.
Lorenzi Diamond has representatives in various countries including Japan, Taiwan, the United States, Belgium, Australia and China, Even Zohar said.
